# Jubilees Chapter 28 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob's marriages and the birth of his twelve sons

---

**28:1** During the forty-third jubilee, second year, first week — Jacob arrived in the east, in the country where his uncle Laban lived, and he moved in with him.

**28:2** Before a month was out, Laban said: "You can't work for me for free — what do you want as your wages?"

**28:3** Laban had two daughters. The older one was Leah, the younger was Rachel. Leah had gentle eyes, but Rachel was strikingly beautiful.

**28:4** Jacob had fallen for Rachel. "I'll work seven years for you," he told Laban, "in exchange for Rachel."

**28:5** "Better you than some stranger," Laban said. "Stay."

**28:6** Jacob worked the seven years, and they felt like nothing — he was so in love.

**28:7** In the forty-fourth jubilee, first week, first year, Jacob went to Laban: "My time is up. Give me Rachel so we can be married."

**28:8** Laban threw a feast. But that night, he sneaked in his older daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob instead. Jacob didn't realize until morning.

**28:9** When he saw it was Leah, he was furious. "What have you done to me? I worked for Rachel! Why did you trick me?"

**28:10** Laban shrugged. "Here we don't give the younger daughter before the older — it's just not done. Finish out this wedding week, and then I'll give you Rachel too, for another seven years of work."

**28:11** Jacob gritted his teeth and finished the week. In the second year of that same week of the forty-fourth jubilee, Laban gave him Rachel as his wife.

**28:12** Jacob loved Rachel far more than Leah. He worked out the remaining seven years.

**28:13** God saw that Leah was unloved, and he opened her womb. Rachel, meanwhile, remained barren.

**28:14** Leah's first son was born on the fourteenth day of the ninth month in year one. She named him Reuben.

**28:15** Year three brought Simeon. Year four, Levi. Year five, Judah.

**28:16** Rachel watched her sister produce child after child while she had none. Her jealousy became unbearable. She turned on Jacob: "Give me children! If you don't, I might as well be dead."

**28:17** Jacob shot back: "Do you think I'm God? It's God who has closed your womb, not me."

**28:18** Rachel tried a different approach: "Take Bilhah, my servant. Sleep with her. Whatever child she bears will count as mine — she'll be my surrogate."

**28:19** Bilhah became Jacob's concubine-wife, and she bore him a son. Rachel named the boy Dan.

**28:20** Bilhah bore a second son, and Rachel named him Naphtali.

**28:21** When Leah realized she had stopped getting pregnant, she gave Jacob her own servant Zilpah as a wife. Zilpah bore a son, and Leah named him Gad.

**28:22** Zilpah had another son, and Leah named him Asher.

**28:23** During the wheat harvest, Reuben stumbled upon some mandrakes growing in a field and brought them home to his mother. Rachel saw them and begged Leah: "Please — let me have some of Reuben's mandrakes."

**28:24** Leah's bitterness surfaced: "You've already taken my husband — now you want my son's mandrakes too?" Rachel bargained: "All right — Jacob can sleep with you tonight if you give them to me."

**28:25** That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah met him at the gate: "You're coming in with me tonight — I bought your time with Reuben's mandrakes." And he did.

**28:26** God heard Leah's prayer that night, and she became pregnant again — a fifth son. She named him Issachar.

**28:27** Then came a sixth son: Zebulun.

**28:28** And finally a daughter: Dinah.

**28:29** Then at last God remembered Rachel. He heard her and opened her womb. She got pregnant and bore a son, and named him Joseph.

**28:30** "God has lifted my shame," she said. And she prayed: "LORD, give me one more son."

---

*PNEUMA notes: The births are presented in a compressed chronological sequence. The mandrake scene (vv.23-25) is rendered to capture its mix of desperation and dark humor. Rachel's final prayer in v.30 foreshadows Benjamin. The dynamic rendering emphasizes Laban's cunning and Jacob's powerlessness in this household.*
